questions: Do the five sensors resolve the line with a clean, monotonic signal, or do adjacent sensors read the tape too coarsely (for example, a 10 mm spacing too wide or too narrow for a 25 mm tape)?
Does the sensor forward offset of 0.04 m cause excessive lag or overshoot for the Integrator's controller gains, or does it help?
Is the wheel track of 0.12 m giving enough turn authority on the tightest bend, or does the robot saturate the wheels?
Does mass 0.6 kg give acceleration that is useful, or do the wheels slip under full base_speed?
Which geometry parameter would you change first to reduce steering oscillation or line loss?

intent: Establish a symmetric, low-mass baseline with five closely spaced 12 mm sensors ahead of the axle, so the Integrator has a clean platform to tune. Next iteration, adjust sensor spacing and forward offset based on how well the centre sensors resolve the line at high speed, and adjust wheel track and mass based on whether the robot oscillates or slides on bends.
learning: No prior race evidence. Hypotheses to test: (H1) A 10 mm sensor spacing with 12 mm footprints gives adequate line resolution across the 25 mm tape. (H2) Sensors placed further forward (y around 0.06 to 0.07 m) reduce oscillation at speed but may reduce signal stability on tight bends. (H3) A wider wheel track (around 0.15 m) reduces slip-induced line loss at the cost of agility. (H4) Lower mass improves completion time without hurting off-track margin, because body width currently has no effect on the limit.
rationale: This is iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry or Integrator feedback yet. The design is a neutral baseline built from the contract's physics, not from evidence. Five sensors at 10 mm spacing (x = +0.02 to -0.02 m) with 12 mm footprints give a tape-covering window of about 25 mm, so at least two or three sensors read the line at any offset. Weights are proportional to sensor x (+2, +1, 0, -1, -2), which matches the sign convention: sensors on the left (positive x) carry positive weight and steer left when the tape is under them. Sensors sit 0.04 m ahead of the axle to reduce the lag between sensing and steering on bends. Wheel track 0.12 m and wheel radius 0.035 m give a moderate turn response and a higher ground speed per rotation. Mass 0.6 kg keeps acceleration high for the 1.5 m/s average-speed requirement. Body width 0.12 m sits well inside the off-track limit (it stays at the 0.06 m floor until the width exceeds about 0.19 m). Body length 0.18 m is a neutral envelope with no direct dynamic effect. Expected result: the robot should complete the development tracks with few line losses, though I expect rms_error to be dominated by how fast the Integrator's controller can turn at the tighter bends.
